description:
Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza is warning of a looming healthcare emergency as a worsening power crisis threatens life-saving services.
Hospital officials say three generators have failed, leaving the facility dependent on a small number of ageing machines running continuously for more than two years amid fuel shortages and a lack of spare parts.
The crisis has already forced operating rooms to suspend services, while intensive care, neonatal and dialysis units remain at risk of shutting down at any moment.
Al-Aqsa Hospital is the only government-run hospital serving more than 500,000 people in central Gaza.
Administrators say the remaining generators are under mounting pressure, with no reliable access to replacement parts or maintenance equipment.
Doctors warn that every passing day brings the hospital closer to a full-scale healthcare collapse, threatening thousands of patients who rely on critical treatment.

David Des Roches, a former Pentagon and NATO operations director and professor at the Near East South Asia Center for Strategic Studies, told Al Jazeera that Russia's deadly airstrikes on Ukrainian residential areas appear to be deliberate targeting rather than collateral damage. 
He noted that while three possibilities exist—a direct targeted strike, debris from an intercepted missile, or a malfunctioning interceptor—the scale of destruction and Russia's pattern of behavior make deliberate targeting the most likely explanation. 
Des Roches said Russia is likely using high-trajectory missiles that are nearly impossible to intercept, such as the Oreshnik missile, which is basically indefensible because it goes so high and comes in so fast. 
He characterized Russia's actions as tactical retaliation for Ukraine's attacks on Russian logistics and airfields, not a strategic shift.

Israeli forces continued operations across southern Lebanon, killing at least five people in renewed strikes on Nabatieh and surrounding areas.
Artillery shelling and air raids also hit multiple towns as Israel says it will proceed with its military campaign in the south.
The escalation comes despite claims by US President Donald Trump that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to pause hostilities.
Trump also said he urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to avoid a major raid on Beirut, prompting questions over the status of negotiations.
Israeli strikes have also damaged a Lebanese Civil Defence centre and repeatedly hit areas near Jabal Amel Hospital in Tyre.
Medical facilities report severe damage, with parts of the hospital infrastructure no longer operational and emergency services under strain.
At least four people were killed in the latest strike near the hospital, with dozens more injured amid ongoing bombardment in the region.

description:
A wave of Russian air strikes across Ukraine has killed at least 11 people and injured more than 100. 
Kyiv was the worst hit, where at least four people were killed and dozens more injured after a strike on a residential building caused partial collapse and left residents possibly trapped under rubble. 
Ukraine says multiple cities were targeted, including Kharkiv and Dnipro, where seven people were killed and residential areas and infrastructure were damaged. 
Russia’s Ministry of Defence says the “massive strike” used “high-precision weapons” and targeted Kyiv and the regions of Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk, as well as energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military. 
Emergency crews continue search and rescue operations amid widespread destruction in Kyiv neighbourhoods. 
Authorities say shelters had been crowded overnight as warnings of a major attack circulated in advance. 

Al Jazeera’s Audrey McAlpine reports from Kyiv.
